title: Hirt's job at D'Antoni's Curly's Corner
summary: Hirt left WWL for a club on St. Charles; D'Antoni complained about the loudness and a rough scene made Netto want to leave.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, when Jumbo left, WWL if you remember that, I was playing with him then. No, I don't remember it. Because he signed up with, with, with, uh, Vicar, well, D'Antoni, when he opened up that place on, when he opened up that boxing club there that's on St. Charles and Poitras.
You know which club he's talking about, Dick? Curly's?

Curly's. Curly's Corner. He, uh, whatever. He, uh, he went in there and the first night we were in there, but you know how loud Jumbo blew. He told Jumbo, he says, for Christ's sake you're playing so loud I can't even think. So, uh, Jumbo says, Sarah, he says, I got a contract with this guy. He says, you gotta pay me. He says, he can't find me. He says, after all I quit WWL and everything else. So, here comes two ladies down in the bar over there and some guy's wife, I don't know who it was, D'Antoni went over there. He says, look, he said, I'm gonna tell you right down, there ain't no hoes gonna be around over here. And, uh, they had quite a big of them. Godfrey Hirsch. Yeah, I believe it was Godfrey. I said, Godfrey, I said, we better get the hell out of here. I said, they're gonna wind up there and somebody's gonna shoot somebody and I said, they're gonna miss them and hit us. How long had you known Godfrey at that point? I knew Godfrey from back when I was, he used to play a night when he was going to school. He played drums with Godfrey. He used to play a night when he was going to school. He played drums. He was playing drums with us, yeah. When Crum would take off a night now and then, Godfrey would play for us.
